name: RX

hero.title: `items().sort()` just mutated your state. `sortBy` does not.
hero.lede: Filter, sort, group, search, sum: 43 functions in one package. Pass a signal and get a live computed back; pass a plain array and get an array. Derived lists become one line each, they never mutate the source, and `pipe` runs a whole chain as one reactive node.

items.title: Never mutates the source
items.text: `sortBy` sorts a copy and compares numbers as numbers, so `[1, 10, 2]` comes back `[1, 2, 10]`. A hand-written `items().sort()` inside a `computed` reorders the signal's own array.

items.title: One function, two modes
items.text: `filter(users, fn)` with a signal returns a `Computed` that re-derives when `users` changes. `filter(list, fn)` with an array returns an array. Same import on the server, in tests and in components.

items.title: `pipe` is one node
items.text: `pipe(products, inStock, byPrice, top3)` is one computed: one subscription, one recompute per change. Three separate calls make three nodes and three hops.

items.title: Timers that clean up
items.text: `debounce(query, 300)` gives a signal that settles 300 ms after the last keystroke. Inside a component its effect and pending timer go away on unmount.

difference.title: Three computeds, one bug, or one `pipe`.

before.label: by hand
before.caption: A computed per step. Forget the `[...]` copy and the sort reorders `inStock`'s cached array in place.
before.code:
const inStock = computed(() =>
  products().filter((p) => p.stock > 0))
const byPrice = computed(() =>
  [...inStock()].sort((a, b) => a.price - b.price))
const top3 = computed(() => byPrice().slice(0, 3))

after.label: with @pyreon/rx
after.caption: One computed for the chain. Each stage is a plain function; rx helpers on plain arrays return plain arrays.
after.code:
import { pipe, sortBy, take } from '@pyreon/rx'

const top3 = pipe(
  products,
  (items) => items.filter((p) => p.stock > 0),
  (items) => sortBy(items, 'price'),
  (items) => take(items, 3),
)

top3()  // ['Desk lamp', 'Monitor arm', 'Mechanical keyboard']
products.update((ps) => [...ps, plantPot])
top3()  // ['Plant pot', 'Desk lamp', 'Monitor arm']

comingFrom.title: A filtered, debounced list without a subscription.
comingFrom.note: `@pyreon/rx` is not RxJS. RxJS is push-based streams over time: events, HTTP, cancellation with `switchMap`, schedulers, backpressure. `@pyreon/rx` is pull-based derivation of the current value of a signal, plus `debounce`, `throttle`, `scan` and `distinct` for signals. Keep RxJS for event streams; for "a list that depends on other state" this is less code. For requests, use `@pyreon/query`.

demo.title: Search, sort and group a live list.
demo.text: One `pipe` over a products signal: search, sort and group. The counter shows how many times the pipe recomputed: once per change, however many stages it has.
demo.spec: A products signal (12 rows: name, category, price) and three control signals: a search query, a sort key (name | price) with a direction (asc | desc), and a grouping (none | category). One `pipe(products, (xs) => search(xs, query(), ['name', 'cat']), (xs) => sortBy(xs, key(), dir()), (xs) => grouped() ? groupBy(xs, 'cat') : xs)` whose first stage increments a recompute counter; the counter goes up by exactly one per input change. The code panel shows that real call shape: rx helpers are called with the array first inside each stage. It must not show curried forms such as `rx.search('q', keys)` or `rx.sortBy('name')`, which do not exist.

features.title: 43 functions, grouped the way you think.

items.name: Aggregation
items.text: `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `average`, `reduce`, `every`, `some`. `sum`, `min`, `max` and `average` take a key or a selector.

items.name: `search(source, query, keys)`
items.text: Case-insensitive match across the fields you name; the query can be a signal.

items.name: `debounce` / `throttle`
items.text: Signals that settle; torn down with the component, or `.dispose()` outside one.

items.name: `scan` / `distinct`
items.text: Running totals, and a signal that only notifies on a real change.

items.name: `combine` / `zip` / `merge`
items.text: Join several signals: one function over their values, pairs by index, or one concatenated list.

items.name: `pipe`
items.text: A whole chain in one computed node, typed stage by stage up to seven.

items.name: `rx.*` or named imports
items.text: A namespace for dot-notation, named exports for tree-shaking: the same functions.

recipes.title: A dashboard tile from one source
recipes.text: Totals, counts per category and groups, each a live computed over the same signal.

recipes.title: Selected rows that survive a refresh
recipes.text: The intersection of what is selected and what is still in the list, live on both sides.

limits.title: Pass the signal, not its value
limits.text: `filter(users, fn)` is live. `filter(users(), fn)` runs once and never updates, because detection is `typeof source === 'function'`.

limits.title: Outside a component, dispose timers
limits.text: `debounce`, `throttle`, `distinct` and `scan` own an effect. In a component or `effectScope` it is torn down for you; elsewhere call `.dispose()`.

limits.title: `search` reads string fields
limits.text: `search` matches only fields whose value is a string, so a number or a nested object in `keys` never matches. Map it to a string field first, or use `filter` with your own test.

limits.title: Not a stream library
limits.text: No `switchMap`, no schedulers, no cancellation. For events over time and request racing, RxJS still fits; for server data, `@pyreon/query`.

faq.a: No. It is collection helpers, lodash-style, that understand signals. The benchmark races it against a hand-written `computed` and Solid's `createMemo`; RxJS appears there only as scale context, because it solves a different problem.

faq.q: Is it slower than writing the computed myself?
faq.a: Filter, map and sum measure level with or ahead of a hand-written computed. `pipe` of three stages and `sortBy` read 1.03× behind a hand computed, `groupBy` 1.02× behind, but the harness prints medians without confidence intervals there, so the record gives them no verdict.
For a chain of two or more steps that nothing else reads in between. It builds one node instead of one per step. If you need an intermediate result elsewhere, keep that step as its own computed.

faq.q: Does it work on iOS and Android?
faq.a: The package is in the shared tier: supported transforms, namespaced or imported by name, lower to native collection operations, and an unsupported one warns by name. Native targets are experimental.

benchmarks.rival: vs a hand-written `computed` and Solid `createMemo` · 1,000 rows, bun/JavaScriptCore
benchmarks.h: A pipeline costs one node, not N.
benchmarks.p: The record's fair peer is the computed you would write without rx; RxJS appears in the harness only as scale context, not as a race. `pipe` fusing three stages into one node is an exact count. For three rows the harness prints medians with no confidence interval, so the record gives no verdict.
